drills.q: Your colleague writes =VLOOKUP(A2, Sheet2!A:D, 3, FALSE) and someone inserts a column in Sheet2. What happens, and what's the one-formula modern fix?
drills.a: VLOOKUP returns data from the WRONG column silently -- col_index 3 is now a different field. Fix: =XLOOKUP(A2, Sheet2!A:A, Sheet2!C:C) -- lookup and return arrays are independent, so inserts cannot break the mapping. Bonus: multi-column return XLOOKUP(A2, names, B2:D6) spills all three.

drills.q: A report shows =UNIQUE(Dept) with #SPILL! that worked yesterday. Diagnose and fix.
drills.a: Something now occupies a cell inside the spill's claimed range (an inserted row/column with content, or a new adjacent value). Spills refuse to overwrite -- by design. Fix: clear the blocker; don't re-type the formula.

drills.q: Write a running total with no dragged formula, and name the general mechanism.
drills.a: =SCAN(0, C2:C6, LAMBDA(acc, v, acc + v)) -- SCAN emits one value per input element with an accumulator LAMBDA; the whole column spills from one cell. Generalizes: running max, running concatenation, any accumulating logic by changing the LAMBDA body.

drills.q: Produce a live top-3 salespeople list in one formula chain.
drills.a: =TAKE(SORTBY(names, sales, -1), 3): SORTBY sorts names by the (hidden) sales column descending, TAKE slices the first 3. Updates automatically as source changes -- no manual re-sort.

drills.q: Why is =SUM(C2:C500000)+AVERAGE(C2:C500000)+MAX(C2:C500000) a problem, and what's the fix?
drills.a: Three full passes over 500k rows -- each sub-expression is a separate scan. Fix: =LET(rng, C2:C500000, SUM(rng)+AVERAGE(rng)+MAX(rng)) binds once; with names for each aggregate it also reads better. LET is a performance primitive, not just style.

drills.q: Define CalcTotal(price, tax) = price * (1 + tax) as a workbook function without VBA.
drills.a: =LAMBDA(price, tax, price * (1 + tax)) typed in a cell, then Name Manager -> New -> name 'CalcTotal' -> Refers to: the LAMBDA. Now =CalcTotal(150, 0.08) works anywhere in the workbook like a built-in. LAMBDAs recurse via their own saved name -- Excel is Turing-complete without macros.

drills.q: A 400k-row SUMIFS sheet recalculates on every keystroke and takes seconds. Name the diagnosis order.
drills.a: 1) Volatile functions: INDIRECT/OFFSET/TODAY/NOW chains force full recalc -- replace with structured refs. 2) Whole-column references vs Table ranges. 3) File format: .xlsx -> .xlsb (binary, smaller/faster). 4) Structural: move the aggregation to Power Query/model. 'Excel is slow, use Python' skips the two cheap fixes.

drills.q: Replace the classic LEFT/FIND/MID email-domain extraction with one modern formula.
drills.a: =TEXTAFTER(A2, "@") — one readable function, live-updating, no nested FIND arithmetic. For multi-delimiter splits: TEXTSPLIT. Both are live formulas unlike Text-to-Columns, which must be re-run after source changes.

drills.q: Why does =IF(A2>120000,"Senior",IF(A2>80000,"Mid",IF(A2>50000,"Junior","Entry"))) get replaced, and write the replacement.
drills.a: Nested IF past 2-3 levels is parenthesis-counting soup. =IFS(A2>120000,"Senior", A2>80000,"Mid", A2>50000,"Junior", TRUE,"Entry") reads top-to-bottom; the final TRUE is the else catch-all.

drills.q: A teammate on Excel 2016 receives your FILTER/UNIQUE workbook. What do they see, and what question should you have asked first?
drills.a: #NAME? errors and @-implicit-intersection mangling: 2016 has no dynamic array engine. First question: 'what builds does the team run?' If 2016, the answer was Power Query + INDEX/MATCH, not spills. Version discipline is a production skill, not trivia.

drills.q: Weekly-refresh cleaning (trim, split, casing) — why Power Query over formulas for the durable version?
drills.a: PQ steps are documented, inspectable in a pane, refreshable, and testable — the logic lives in named steps, not inside cells. Formula-tier (TRIM/TEXTSPLIT/PROPER) is for the ad-hoc one-off pass. The tier choice IS the answer: one-off vs weekly.

drills.q: Name the three tiers of modern Excel and what each owns — one sentence each.
drills.a: Power Query owns ETL (clean/shape/merge before the grid); the Data Model owns relationships and measures (star schema, DAX); the formula tier owns live ad-hoc analysis and self-updating report blocks. Production failures are boundary violations — ETL in formulas, modeling in mega-formulas.
